assumptions: The stated requests are interpreted as the accepted point demand estimates: North 1800 kg and South 1.2 tonnes, with no uplift for rainfall because no uncertainty response function or bound is supplied.
The standard metric conversion 1 tonne = 1000 kg is used, so South demand is 1200 kg and total accepted demand is 3000 kg.
A trip may carry up to 600 kg, and the proposed plan uses full 600 kg loads.
The crew-hours limit applies only to loading as quantified in the brief; travel time, unloading time, and route duration are not modeled because they are not supplied.
Trip counts are integer decisions. Pack-level integrality cannot be enforced because pack weights and inventory counts are absent.

baseline.description: Directly satisfy both accepted requests after converting all quantities to kilograms.
baseline.result: North 1800 kg (3 trips), South 1200 kg (2 trips), total 3000 kg (5 trips), using 7.5 crew-hours; feasible under all stated numerical limits.

candidate_models: Deterministic integer trip-allocation model using accepted point demands; usable with the supplied data.
Robust or stochastic allocation model for rainfall-driven demand uncertainty; not identifiable because no uncertainty set, scenarios, probabilities, or rainfall-demand response is supplied.
Priority-weighted shortage model; not identifiable because no shelter priorities or shortage costs are supplied.
claims: Verified from local input and arithmetic: the accepted point demands total 3000 kg.
Verified from local input and arithmetic: the proposed 3-North/2-South trip allocation exactly meets accepted point demands and satisfies stated trip and crew constraints.
Verified from local input: rainfall is uncontrollable and only correlation, not causation, is stated.
Proposed but not operationally verified: the sealed-pack inventory can be assembled into the exact kilogram allocations and safely dispatched.

data_findings: Accepted demand is North 1800 kg, South 1200 kg, total 3000 kg.
Five full trips provide exactly 3000 kg and require 7.5 crew-hours.
A request-proportional exact allocation is North 3 trips = 1800 kg and South 2 trips = 1200 kg.
The plan leaves 1 nominal trip unused, 600 kg of nominal trip-capacity availability unused, and 0.5 crew-hours unused; the sixth trip cannot be loaded within the stated crew-hour limit.
No quantified rainfall-to-demand mapping, uncertainty interval, shelter priority, shortage penalty, pack size, inventory count, travel time, or route constraint appears in the brief.
experiment_design: Before dispatch, independently recount full loads as 3 North trips and 2 South trips and verify each load mass is at most 600 kg.
Check source labels and manifest units, recompute South 1.2 tonnes as 1200 kg, and reconcile total manifest mass to 3000 kg.
Recompute resource use from the dispatch sheet: 5 trips <= 6 and 7.5 crew-hours <= 8.
Confirm sealed-pack counts and per-pack masses permit exactly 1800 kg and 1200 kg without opening packs.
Obtain an updated rainfall/attendance assessment from an authorized human; if accepted demand changes, mark the allocation stale and rerun from Task 1 rather than editing the final report.
Record verifier identity, timestamp, weigh/count evidence, manifest identifiers, and explicit dispatch approval.
falsification_tests: Attempt a sixth loaded trip: 6*1.5 = 9 crew-hours, which falsifies feasibility under the 8 crew-hour limit.
Reduce the plan to four full trips: 4*600 = 2400 kg, which is 600 kg short of total accepted demand.
Swap to North 2 trips or South 1 trip: the affected shelter becomes 600 kg short, falsifying demand satisfaction.
If any pack count or measured load cannot realize 1800 kg North and 1200 kg South within 600 kg per trip, falsify operational feasibility and do not dispatch under this plan.
If a freshness hash differs, falsify the current handoff status and restart at the earliest affected stage.

constraints: x_N and x_S are nonnegative integers.
600*x_N >= 1800 and 600*x_S >= 1200 for zero unmet accepted demand.
notes: The exact solution consumes all crew-feasible freight capacity: 5 trips * 600 kg = 3000 kg.
Correlation between rainfall and historical attendance is not treated as a causal coefficient or used to alter demand.
Pack-level feasibility remains a human validation item because individual sealed-pack mass and available pack count are missing.
formalization.objective: Minimize total unmet accepted demand; among zero-unmet-demand solutions, minimize loaded trips.
parameters: h = 1.5 crew-hours/trip and H = 8 crew-hours available.
r = 75 mm forecast rainfall, retained as non-controllable context without a supplied demand-response coefficient.
units: One-row unit summary: source quantities | accepted conversion | normalized quantities | operational rates = North 1800 kg; South 1.2 tonnes | 1 tonne = 1000 kg | North 1800 kg, South 1200 kg, total 3000 kg | truck 600 kg/trip, labor 1.5 crew-hours/trip, rainfall 75 mm.
variables: x_N: integer number of trips allocated to Shelter North.
x_S: integer number of trips allocated to Shelter South.
q_N = 600*x_N: kilograms allocated to North under full-load assumption.
q_S = 600*x_S: kilograms allocated to South under full-load assumption.
Rainfall is not a decision variable.

human_gates: Gate 1: an authorized planner accepts the Task 1 interpretation that requests are point demands and approves the 1 tonne = 1000 kg conversion.
Gate 2: operations verifies pack inventory, pack weights, load weights, vehicle availability, crew scheduling, and manifests against the proposed allocation.
Gate 3: an authorized risk owner reviews current rainfall/attendance information and decides whether the point-demand plan remains acceptable despite unquantified uncertainty.
Gate 4: a dispatcher records explicit approval only after freshness and operational evidence checks pass; no human approval is present in the supplied inputs.
reality_constraints: North request: 1800 kg; South request: 1.2 tonnes = 1200 kg.
Truck capacity: 0.6 tonnes = 600 kg per trip.
Each loaded trip consumes 1.5 crew-hours; at most 8 crew-hours are available.
The crew limit permits at most floor(8/1.5) = 5 loaded trips, making crew capacity tighter than the 6-trip availability limit.
Forecast rainfall is 75 mm and uncontrollable; its quantitative effect on demand is unspecified.
Historical shelter attendance is correlated with rainfall, but no causal study is provided.
Work was restricted to the isolated repository and local listed inputs; network, MCP, remotes, parent directories, credentials, and historical material were not used.
requirements: Task 1: build a requirement trace and identify controllable decisions.
Task 2: propose an allocation using the accepted demand estimate, unit conversion, and demand interpretation from Task 1.
Task 3: specify pre-dispatch validation of the allocation.
Allocate sealed water packs between Shelter North and Shelter South for the next 12 hours.
Respect at most 6 available trips, 0.6 tonnes truck capacity per trip, 1.5 crew-hours per loaded trip, and at most 8 crew-hours.
Include a one-row unit summary in the final handoff even if no model is selected.
Treat rainfall as demand-uncertainty information, not as an allocator-controlled decision.
Do not infer causation from the stated correlation between historical attendance and rainfall.
Dependency trace: Task 1 accepted units and demand interpretation -> Task 2 allocation -> Task 3 validation -> human dispatch approval.
robustness_tests: Crew-hour slack is only 0.5 hours; any additional loading labor exceeding 0.5 hours makes the five-trip plan infeasible under the stated shift limit.
Freight slack across the crew-feasible five trips is 0 kg; any accepted demand increase makes exact service infeasible without changing resources or assumptions.
One nominal trip is available but not crew-feasible; adding at least 1 crew-hour would raise the 8-hour limit to the 9 crew-hours required for six loaded trips.
Rainfall sensitivity cannot be quantified from the brief; scenario testing must wait for an approved demand range or response model.
selected_model: Deterministic integer trip-allocation model using accepted point demands
self_reported_limitations: No external sources were consulted, so the tonne conversion is used as the standard metric definition and is explicitly exposed as an accepted conversion assumption/gate.
The allocation is validated only against supplied numerical constraints, not against physical inventory, routes, timing, or human approval.
No causal or predictive rainfall model can be justified from the supplied correlation statement.
No status is marked FINAL; operational dispatch remains gated.
